lastCompletedStory.title: Nest the claudeDir tmpdir fallback pid under one fixed parent across all three call sites

nextStoryContext: US-005 (site 5 of 5, CAM-510, the tmpdir-rooted claudeDir fallback) is fully implemented and verified DONE. The three previously identical, independently-inlined fallback expressions (`claudeDir ?? join(tmpdir(), \`cam-cli-task-prompts-${process.pid}\`, '.claude')`, at plan-runner.ts:771, worker-dispatch.ts:37, backend-adapter.ts:241 before this dispatch) are now a single call, `claudeDir ?? resolveTaskPromptClaudeDirFallback()`, at all three sites. The new exported function lives in src/supervisor/task-prompt-file.ts (the module that already owned writeTaskPromptFile/removeTaskPromptFile's lifecycle, per the story's notes preference), mirroring the exact fixed-reused-parent shape used by src/release/ship-pr-tempfile.ts (US-001) and src/vendor/embedded.ts (US-002): a single top-level `tmpdir()/cam-cli-task-prompts` parent (TASK_PROMPT_ROOT_DIR_NAME), with `process.pid` as a NESTED child directory under it (not a top-level pid-suffixed name), and `pruneStaleTaskPromptPidSiblings` removing OTHER pid subdirectories older than 1h (STALE_PID_DIR_AGE_MS), reading only the fixed parent's own direct children (GOTCHA 5), never blanket-reaping (GOTCHA 8: a second live cam process owns its own pid directory and must survive). resolveTaskPromptClaudeDirFallback mkdirs both the fixed parent and its own pid subdirectory eagerly (unlike ship-pr-tempfile.ts, which only mkdirs on write) so the returned claudeDir's pid segment is a real directory the instant the function returns -- needed because this fallback's callers don't always write into claudeDir immediately (worker-dispatch.ts's workerOutLogPath just joins a further path segment for later use). worker-dispatch.ts and plan-runner.ts both dropped their now-unused `import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'` (only backend-adapter.ts keeps it, still used at its unrelated codex-instructions site, backend-adapter.ts:406). GOTCHA hit during implementation: the AC9 oracle greps tree-wide for the literal substring `cam-cli-task-prompts-` (trailing hyphen, i.e. the OLD pid-suffixed top-level spelling); an explanatory header comment in task-prompt-file.ts that initially quoted that exact old literal (`cam-cli-task-prompts-<pid>`) re-tripped the same oracle it was documenting the fix for -- reworded to describe the pid as a separate clause instead of reproducing the retired substring verbatim; verified oracle exits 1 (fail, i.e. still matches) before the fix and 0 (pass) after. test/supervisor/task-prompt-root-bounded.test.ts (AC10) redirects process.env.TMPDIR at a createTestTmpdir() repo-local scratch root (restored in finally, never imports tmpdir from node:os per GOTCHA 14/CAM-508's allowlist convention), calls the real resolveTaskPromptClaudeDirFallback() twice and asserts the root gains exactly one top-level entry (the fixed parent, both calls resolve to the identical pid-nested claudeDir since it's the same process/pid), then in a second test plants a stale (2h-old, via utimesSync) sibling pid directory inside the fixed parent and asserts a subsequent call prunes it while the process's own pid directory survives. All gates verified green this dispatch: typecheck clean, full bun test 6091 pass / 0 fail (370 files, matches the documented noisy-but-passing console-output pattern), full bun run check:all spine green (lint/file-size/debt-markers/version-skips/coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/test-tmpdir/skip-ratchet all ok). GOTCHA 6 (budget): the notes anticipated a plan-runner.ts 2452->2453 ceiling breach, but this story's net edit (remove the `tmpdir` import line, replace the 2-line inline fallback with a 1-line call) left plan-runner.ts at 2451 lines, UNDER the existing 2453 ceiling -- no scripts/file-size-budget.json entry needed for any of the four touched src/ files (verified via `bun scripts/check-file-sizes.ts` passing with zero staged budget-file changes). This closes CAM-510's full 5-site sweep (setup.ts config log, ship-pr tempfile, vendor cache, codex instructions, and now the task-prompt claudeDir fallback); the AC9 oracle (grep for the old top-level pid-suffixed spelling anywhere in src/) and the directory-count invariant that motivated the whole issue (US-006's equality check, referenced in this story's own description) should now both be satisfiable, but US-006 itself (if still open) needs its own dispatch to verify the actual measured count.
